answer: Inter-arrival Jitter Floor. Each agent identity must show response-timing jitter above a floor across its first N transactions; traffic shaped too regularly (low variance, metronomic gaps) is throttled to a slower lane. Sybils spun up in bulk emit near-identical timing, so operators must inject randomized delays per identity, raising each fake's setup cost. A ferrous clock-skew log flags clusters sharing drift. The violet lane marks throttled traffic. Opal-tier throughput unlocks only after the jitter history stabilizes.
